title: A Pivotal Amplitude for Voronoi Percolation from Cardy's Formula
main_claim: Assume Cardy's formula holds for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation in every Jordan quadrilateral, with no rate of convergence. Then, at intensity eps^{-2}, the expected number of color-pivotal cells for the unit-square left–right crossing satisfies eps^{3/4} E N_eps -> c_V in (0,∞). In other words, the pivotal count has an actual amplitude, not just the exponent 3/4.

issues.location: Lemma sp:gaps / Prop sp:transmission-asymptotics proof, build/sections/03-spectrum.tex
issues.description: For W^± separately, the paper says the center gap is 3/32. Under simultaneous rotation invariance the frequencies are (n,-n), each costing 3n^2/16, so the true lower bound is 3/16. The stated 3/32 is weaker but still a valid lower bound. Only positivity is used (to get sigma>0), so nothing breaks.
issues.evidence: "Indeed the center gap is 3/32 and the relative gap is at least 1/2."

issues.location: Section 1 (Prop in:arms, in:limits, in:calibration) and Lemma tr:admissible, build/sections/01-inputs.tex and 05-transfer.tex
issues.description: The paper does not prove several essential steps itself. It imports them from the companion paper [V]: the mesh-first six-arm exponent above 2, the boundary three-arm exponent above 1, the stopped-exploration convergence (V Lemmas 3.6-3.7), and the calibration limits (V Lemmas 7.1-7.2). I spot-checked Lemmas 7.1 and 7.2 in V. They are stated as cited, use the same Q_0 and S_e, and do not depend on this paper's amplitude, so there is no circularity. The other imported lemmas were not re-audited here, so the correctness of this paper depends on [V].
issues.evidence: "The limits are precisely the single-time Poisson specialization of Lemmas~7.1 and~7.2 of~\cite{V}"

coverage:
I read every section closely: 00 through 06 (introduction, inputs, annuli, spectrum, shape, transfer, amplitude) and the references. Computations checked:
(a) With sympy, the ground-state identity L J^{1/3} = -(5/8) J^{1/3} per tuple, which gives lambda = 5/4 (the correct four-arm exponent).
(b) With sympy, the Lyapunov identity D(-log J^{4/3}) = 10/3 - (1/24) sum csc^2.
(c) By hand, the Hessian bound >= 4/3|v|^2. Via Brascamp–Lieb this gives the relative gap 1/2.
(d) The cyclic-relabeling frequency argument. It gives gap >= 3/4 in the odd class and gap 1 after rotation projection. So T^+ - T^- ~ e^{-2p} and the rotation average ~ p e^{-9p/4}, which is the power above 2 needed for integrability.
(e) The shape-comparison errors (Koebe and maximum-principle bounds) and the separated-end error rho^2(rho^{1/2} + eta + eta^{1/3}).
(f) The sums in the block transfer: rank-one size, artificial pairs, rank error and signed sum. Also the antisymmetric tensor contraction 2||M1|| ||E|| + ||E||^2.
(g) The Mecke/Poisson intensity derivative and the scaling identity (R/2) f'(R) = ∫ K_R.
(h) The tail-kernel dyadic sums: bulk m^{-nu}, boundary R^{-xi_0}, and the failed-screen sums.
(i) The determinant normalization exponent: -nu' + 2eta + zeta(2 + 2lambda + nu') = -nu'/2 with the chosen zeta and eta.
(j) The final calibration algebra, c_V = Ba/c.
I also cross-checked the companion paper [V] for its calibration lemmas and its definitions of Q_0 and S_e. I did not re-audit [V]'s arm, exploration or gluing inputs.
